note: The floors are the census sizes measured on the run that wrote them, and they are a ratchet
rather than a guess. A layer that reads fewer rows than its floor exits 3, not 0.
EVERY CITATION IN insights.pairing.tsv OPENS WITH `Dn · `, naming the divergence below it
falls under. A row whose citation carries no number, or a number this file does not define, is
a defect. The split is countable off the run's own artifact:
F='| \(absent\|divergent\|extra\|extra-cited\|unclassified\) |'
grep -c "$F" planning/fidelity/insights.ledger.md
grep "$F" planning/fidelity/insights.ledger.md | grep -c '| D[0-9] ·'
ONE FACT DECIDES MOST OF THIS FILE. Three of the mock's four frames are about the SESSION
ANALYST, and this product has no analyst in any form: PRD.md §6 specifies one and nothing in
app/Sources implements it (spec-M22 §3.6). The mock's v-loading is the analyst running, its
v-error is the analyst falling back to a second model, and a third of its v-ideal is the
analyst's own configuration. The brief handles this correctly by asking for `its own
configuration and its last run` rather than for the analyst, so the board draws that panel's
empty state and its two other frames are the BOARD's own load rather than the analyst's.
1. THE ANALYST DOES NOT EXIST. Owner: PRD §6, unimplemented. The three model pop-ups, the
run cadence, the last-run line, the progress frame, the usage-limit banner and the
`Change the order…` action all describe a subsystem with no code behind it. The board
renders `analyst: null` from the route — a member that is PRESENT and null, so the empty
state is drawn from a fact the router stated rather than from a key that failed to parse —
and `Analyse now` is drawn DIM under featureUnbuilt, per DESIGN.md §3.4. Absent rather than
invented: a pop-up listing models nothing will run is a control that lies about the product.
2. THE WINDOW POP-UP IS PARKED. Owner: M22, parked with its reason in plan-M22.md §2.3. The
mock offers `Last 7 days`. The usage log rotates at 8 MiB keeping one generation, so what a
router can answer for is whatever survived; a control offering seven days on a machine
holding two would lie about its own range. The route is fixed at 24 hours and reports
`logHorizon`, the oldest record it actually reached, which is what lets the board say `not
enough history yet` as a measurement rather than a threshold.
3. `Skill and server use, by version` HAS NO DATA BEHIND IT. Owner: M22, declined. Its six
columns and four rows key runs on the version that was live when a call ran. UsageRecord
carries ts, server, tool, ok, ms, cold and the caller, and no version anywhere — not of a
server, not of a skill. DESIGN.md §6 forbids displaying a figure the router does not
observe, so the whole block is absent rather than rendered with a column of dashes.
4. `Analyse now` MOVED FROM THE HEADER TO THE ANALYST PANEL. Owner: M22, deliberate. The mock
puts it in the board head beside the window pop-up. A disabled control belongs beside the
thing it is disabled about — §3.4 asks for a discoverable reason, and the reason is the
analyst's absence, which the panel states in words two lines above the button.
5. THE LOADING AND ERROR FRAMES ARE THE BOARD'S, NOT THE ANALYST'S. Owner: M22, deliberate,
and it follows from 1. The mock's v-loading draws the analyst's progress and its v-error
draws a fallback banner; neither state exists in this product. What the board genuinely has
is a read of GET /insights that has not answered yet, and one that failed — the second
rendered from ControlAPIError, whose routerNotRunning case is its own state per DESIGN.md §5
rather than a generic banner. So every affordance in those two frames is absent, and every
build node in them is an extra.
7. TWO ZERO-AREA FRAMES, AND THEY ARE THE TWO ROWS THIS BOARD EXISTS FOR. Owner: M22,
declared; and a limit of the geometry layer, recorded for M23.
`geometry` reports bar-fill-geminiCLI and bar-fill-duty-docker-mcp as zero-area frames. Both
are correct: a harness that has called nothing and a server that was never opened have a
share of zero, and a fill drawn at zero width is the truthful rendering of that. The row
still carries its label, its track and its value — `0` — which is the brief's criterion.
THE LAYER CANNOT TELL THE TWO CASES APART, which is why this is declared rather than fixed.
Its rule (mock_fidelity.py:574) flags any frame with width or height <= 0, and it exists to
catch a node that FAILED TO LAY OUT. A node that laid out correctly AT zero is
indistinguishable from one that collapsed, because the frame is the only evidence either
way. Nothing in the manifest can express the difference today.
THE ALTERNATIVE WAS REJECTED, and the reason is the acceptance. Omitting the fill node when
the value is zero would clear both findings and make a zero row structurally identical to a
row the router has NO FIGURE for — bar-cursor and bar-codexCLI, which carry no fill because
there is nothing to draw rather than nothing to show. A zero is a measurement and an absence
is not, and the structure is where that distinction is checkable.
8. TWO COPY DIFFERENCES, BOTH FOLLOWING FROM 1 AND 2. Owner: M22, deliberate.
The board subtitle drops the mock's `and what the analyst found in your own session logs`,
because there is no analyst; what it says instead is that every number is counted from calls
this router served, which is the brief's own sentence.
The empty state reads `No calls have been served in the last 24 hours` where the mock reads
`Charts need about a day of calls before they say anything`. The mock states a THRESHOLD and
the build states a MEASUREMENT: `logHorizon` is nil, so the window holds nothing, and the
board says that rather than asserting how much history a chart would need. The mock's
trailing `2 sessions indexed · 18 to go` is the same threshold counted against the analyst,
and is absent under 1.
6. A ZERO ROW DRAWS ITS ZERO AND AN ABSENT COUNT DRAWS NEITHER. Owner: M22, the acceptance.
The brief's own criterion is that a structure dump contains a labelled node per harness
including the ones at zero. It does: bar-geminiCLI carries a bar-fill at zero width, while
bar-cursor and bar-codexCLI have NO bar-fill child at all, because the router has no figure
for them and a zero would be a fabricated finding. That difference is in the structure layer
rather than in prose, which is what makes it checkable.

layers.name: font-weight-face
layers.substitute: A SwiftUI Font is opaque — String(describing: Font.system(size: 13, weight: .semibold)) returns "Font(provider: SwiftUI.FontBox<SwiftUI.Font.SystemProvider>)", with no size, weight or face in it. Confirmed instead by: the TypeToken each text node names is recorded in tokens["type"] at apply time and checked against the measured line box by the type-metrics layer; DesignTokenParityTests pins the eight-role ladder against DESIGN.md; scripts/lint/no-raw-design-values.sh fails any font size that does not come off it. None of the three can see an ancestor .font() winning the cascade, and that residue is what this row is.
